accepted_prior_and_missing_bridges: The base ProviderFailoverPolicy already continued after an empty result and returned the first nonempty result. Its tuple did not retain per-provider outcome records or a typed exhausted state; on total exhaustion it returned the last provider name, an empty hit list, and only the last error. The service could not distinguish all-empty, mixed error/unsuitable, and budget-stop outcomes in persisted query traces. Review also found that two 0.70s empty-provider calls could take 1.403s under a 1.0s run budget because the aggregate deadline did not enter fallback. The candidate preserves ordered policy, applies the remaining deadline to each provider request with cancellation, and persists a distinct max-wall stop. Existing URL/redirect admission remains owned by SearchConstraints and validate_fetch_url; the candidate wires both callers through one raw transport without changing that policy owner. The candidate reads the record's CAS snapshot, applies the same current payload-admission seam used by fresh transport, and refuses unavailable or marker-mismatched snapshots.
